title: A continuous split transfinite module filtration is a direct sum of its factors
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $X$ an $R$-module and $\kappa$ an ordinal (a set, not a proper class). Let $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\kappa}$ be an increasing family of $R$-submodules of $X$ with $X_0=0$ and $X_\kappa=X$. Assume $X_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}X_\beta$ for every nonzero limit ordinal $\lambda\leq\kappa$, and assume that for every $\alpha<\kappa$ the inclusion $X_\alpha\hookrightarrow X_{\alpha+1}$ admits an $R$-linear retraction. Then there exists an $R$-linear isomorphism $X\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha<\kappa}(X_{\alpha+1}/X_\alpha)$, with direct sums as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules] and quotient modules as in [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. No countable-generation or projectivity hypothesis is imposed on the factors.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, lines 20409–20453, with the dévissage of Definition 058U (definition-devissage) indexed by the successor ordinal kappa+1 to include the endpoint.

proof.text:
For each $\alpha<\kappa$ choose a retraction $r_\alpha:X_{\alpha+1}\to X_\alpha$ of the inclusion $j_\alpha:X_\alpha\hookrightarrow X_{\alpha+1}$; this is a set-indexed choice. Put $Q_\alpha=X_{\alpha+1}/X_\alpha$, with quotient map $q_\alpha$ from [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Define
$$s_\alpha:Q_\alpha\longrightarrow X_{\alpha+1},\qquad s_\alpha(q_\alpha(x))=x-j_\alpha r_\alpha(x).$$
This is independent of the representative: replacing $x$ by $x+j_\alpha(a)$ changes the right side by $j_\alpha(a)-j_\alpha r_\alpha j_\alpha(a)=0$. The formula is additive and $R$-linear. Moreover $q_\alpha s_\alpha=\mathrm{id}$, since the subtracted term belongs to $X_\alpha$. Thus every $x\in X_{\alpha+1}$ satisfies $x=j_\alpha r_\alpha(x)+s_\alpha q_\alpha(x)$, and $s_\alpha(z)\in X_\alpha$ implies $z=q_\alpha s_\alpha(z)=0$.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, first sentence of the proof: constructing the inclusions of the successive quotients from condition (3); Tag 058U, definition-devissage, condition (3).

proof.text:
Using the finitely supported families of [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], set $D=\bigoplus_{\alpha<\kappa}Q_\alpha$ and define
$$f:D\longrightarrow X,\qquad f((z_\alpha))=\sum_{\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}(z)}s_\alpha(z_\alpha),$$
where each $X_{\alpha+1}$ is included in $X$. This is a finite sum. On the union of the finite supports of two families the formula gives $f(z+w)=f(z)+f(w)$, and likewise $f(az)=af(z)$, so $f$ is $R$-linear. For $\beta\leq\kappa$, let $D_\beta$ be the submodule of $D$ consisting of the families whose components vanish for $\alpha\geq\beta$. For $\alpha<\beta$ we have $\alpha+1\leq\beta$, hence $s_\alpha(z_\alpha)\in X_\beta$. It follows term by term that $f(D_\beta)\subseteq X_\beta$, and $D_\kappa=D$.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof: the map f and its restrictions f_beta (lines 20417–20427).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-transfinite-successor-generators-surjective] with $A_\alpha=Q_\alpha$ and $t_\alpha=s_\alpha$. Step 1 gives its successor-generation hypothesis; the zero stage and limit continuity are hypotheses of the item. It yields $f(D_\beta)=X_\beta$ for all $\beta\leq\kappa$. Since $D_\kappa=D$ and $X_\kappa=X$, $f$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof lines 20417–20433: definition of f_beta and transfinite induction identifying its image. Generalized to arbitrary successor-generating maps, without requiring them injective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-filtration-successor-maps-independent] with the same $A_\alpha$ and $t_\alpha$. Its hypothesis $s_\alpha(z)\in X_\alpha\Rightarrow z=0$ was proved in step 1 using $q_\alpha s_\alpha=1$. Thus $f$ is injective, including when $\kappa$ is a limit ordinal.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof lines 20435–20453: injectivity from independence of each new summand from its predecessor; equivalent maximal finite-support formulation, for arbitrary maps injective modulo the preceding stage.

proof.text: Steps 3–4 show that $f:D\to X$ is bijective. For each $x\in X$ let $g(x)$ be its unique preimage. If $x,y\in X$ and $a\in R$, then $f(g(x)+g(y))=x+y$ and $f(ag(x))=ax$; uniqueness gives $g(x+y)=g(x)+g(y)$ and $g(ax)=ag(x)$. Hence $g$ is an $R$-linear inverse and provides the required isomorphism $X\cong D=\bigoplus_{\alpha<\kappa}(X_{\alpha+1}/X_\alpha)$, with [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. If $\kappa=0$, the assumptions give $X=0$, $D$ is the empty direct sum, and this same construction is the unique isomorphism between zero modules.

source.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, conclusion of the proof (line 20453).

proof_origin.place: Tag 058V, lemma-direct-sum-devissage, proof lines 20417–20453, with Tag 058U, definition-devissage. The section formula and the maximal-support version of the injectivity argument are written out.
